missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to explain ways of reducing unwanted energy transfers, for example through lubrication and the use of thermal insulation.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson covers wasted and dissipated energy but never explains how to reduce unwanted energy transfers. Lubrication and thermal insulation are not mentioned anywhere.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: The higher the thermal conductivity of a material the higher the rate of energy transfer by conduction across the material.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson does not mention thermal conductivity or how it affects the rate of energy transfer by conduction.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Students should be able to describe how the rate of cooling of a building is affected by the thickness and thermal conductivity of its walls.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson does not discuss the rate of cooling of buildings, wall thickness or wall thermal conductivity.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Required practical activity 2 (physics only): investigate the effectiveness of different materials as thermal insulators and the factors that may affect the thermal insulation properties of a material.
missing_spec_content.why: The required practical on thermal insulators is not covered.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: (HT only) Students should be able to describe ways to increase the efficiency of an intended energy transfer.
missing_spec_content.why: The lesson teaches how to calculate efficiency but not how to increase it.

missing_spec_content.spec_text: Throughout this section on Energy students should be able to calculate the changes in energy involved when a system is changed by: heating, work done by forces, work done when a current flows
missing_spec_content.why: Only the Ek, Ep and Ee equations appear, and only in keyTerms definitions. The lesson does not teach how to calculate energy changes caused by heating, by work done by forces, or by work done when a current flows.

factual_errors.text: By heating: energy flows from a hotter object to a cooler one (conduction, convection). Radiation is a separate pathway.
factual_errors.correction: Energy transfer by heating from a hotter object to a cooler one can also happen by infrared radiation, not only by conduction and convection. Restricting heating to conduction and convection is misleading. The lesson's own lamp caption, '85 J wasted by heating', includes infrared emission.

factual_errors.text: Energy transferred from a hotter object to a cooler one by conduction or convection; always flows from higher to lower temperature. Radiation is a separate pathway.
factual_errors.correction: Heating can also occur by infrared radiation from a hotter object to a cooler one. It is not limited to conduction or convection.

factual_errors.text: most real energy transfers dissipate some energy
factual_errors.correction: The specification states that energy is dissipated in all system changes, not just most of them.

factual_errors.text: It happens in most real devices
factual_errors.correction: Dissipation happens in all system changes, according to the specification text: 'in all system changes energy is dissipated'.
